recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No FHIR-core follow-up is needed for FHIR-18482 unless a future work-group decision reopens the broader Composition/document rendering guidance.
issue_request: FHIR-18482 was a Published FHIR-core narrative change request with resolution Persuasive with Modification. It asked whether resource narrative rules could still vary based on how a resource is referenced and resolved that they do not; the specific requested wording change was to replace "Some resources (e.g. List, Composition) can provide specific rules..." with "Some resources (e.g. List) can provide specific rules...".
initial_application: The Jira comment identifies GH#bf219fb30d, and git commit bf219fb30d4cad44a26f03caa5e79eb6b1c20ee6 changed source/narrative.html to remove Composition from that example. Before this reconciliation, the combined branch did not contain an AutoFHIR audit commit for Issue-Reconcile-Key: FHIR-18482.
additional_context: source/fhir.ini includes Narrative as an infrastructure type and maps narrative/narrative XHTML to the narrative page, so source/narrative.html is in build scope. The current source says "Some resources (e.g., List) can provide specific rules" and the following paragraph says systems SHALL NOT assume a particular rendering context. FHIR-2864 introduced the older broader wording, FHIR-17463 adjusted normative wording in the same paragraph, FHIR-14167 records that non-document Composition follows ordinary resource narrative behavior, FHIR-7404 is background on documents/List narrative handling, and a later FHIR-44047 punctuation edit retained the List-only wording.
reconciliation: Published an intentionally empty no-change audit commit because no current FHIR-core source edit is needed. The current source already reflects the FHIR-18482 resolution and avoids implying that Composition-specific rules make a resource's own narrative obligations depend on whether the resource is contained, bundled, or otherwise referenced.
